scope: Structural disposition of every directory containing non-test Go source; not an exhaustive behavioral or test audit.

Version service boundary, not a verb namespace.

Keep invocation-scoped configuration/session/client construction; move project discovery forwarding into project adapter construction without widening snapshot lifetimes.
Remove per-operation app forwarding and record conversions; action services own operations and resource adapters implement their ports.
Keep provider construction only; relocate resource-specific resolution, enrichment, and workflow decisions with their owners.
One explicit shared resolution-phase implementation; delete app forwarding shims after consumers use the phase contract.
Move lifecycle decisions into datasource actions and API/artifact translations into the resource adapter.
Keep resource-specific publication in its resource workflow and shared file inspection in artifact mechanisms; no generic publication action.
Separate requested schema workflow from native metadata identity/field normalization in one resource adapter.
Datasource list/inspect policy stays resource-specific; move common collection and cache publication into inventory.
Workbook list/inspect behavior stays resource-specific; share collection and cache publication, not external projections.
One common artifact preview mechanism with typed resource port implementations, no app-owned conversion layer.
Keep construction only; place administrative sequencing and provider operations under existing cohesive owners.
Move user/group domain rules to actions and implement their typed provider contracts directly in resources/admin.
Move rule sequencing to permission actions and exact principal resolution/translation to the admin adapter.
Bind the native client directly to value-based action ports, remove catalog forwarding wrappers, and move operations to catalog; retain construction and identity distinctions.
Separate asset attachments from shared definitions by existing domain; eliminate app type-copy adapters.
Keep construction only; named actions own semantics, one provider boundary owns field-catalog/API translation.
Definition bundle sequencing belongs to definition workflows; retain artifact durability and native payload mechanics separately.
Own search selection/recovery in the search service; retain native fallback/identity translation and shared inventory collection at their boundaries.
Share source/coverage/error mechanisms once; put action-typed read ports with resource adapters.
Use the same inventory mechanism as content; keep typed admin readers at their adapter boundary.
Split neutral collection/cache publication from action-typed page adapters; preserve completeness and no-replacement-on-partial-data rules.
Cache workflow owns refresh policy, inventory owns collection/publication, app constructs authenticated executor callbacks.
Authentication workflow owns cross-store ordering and compensation; core auth retains credential/session mechanics.
Terminal prompting is a CLI concern, not composition or credential storage.
Environment workflow owns configuration/credential coordination; auth-status projection belongs to auth; retain constructor binding only in app.
Workspace actions own operations, workspace infrastructure owns rooted inventory/registry mechanics, app constructs dependencies.
Keep constructors in app; workflow and filesystem installation remain separately owned.
Keep update construction; move credential-variable enumeration to config and process launch policy to updater.
Bind shared release records directly and remove copy-only releaseChecker after callers are adapted.
Diagnostics service owns explicit probes and aggregation; app supplies constructed dependencies.
Session owns local overview; shared credential readiness moves to core auth, not action-to-action calls.
Split policy workflows, protected saved-result reads, Cobra binding, policy evaluation, and construction; preserve fail-closed enforcement.
New site-consent workflow owner; config remains canonical persisted authority and app only binds dependencies.
Retain process entry/assembly, not policy algorithms.
Move reusable capture/persistence coordination behind explicit snapshot callbacks; retain top-level defer and renderer binding in app.
Job actions own inspect/wait/recovery, job adapter owns native observations, app constructs providers.
Move accepted-identity receipt/observation coordination into jobmonitor using injected callbacks; resource adapters retain typed acceptance translation and role-sensitive native access.
Resource workflows own completion, resource adapters verify destinations, jobmonitor owns receipt mechanics; remove cross-action completion from app.
Invocation deadline/detach state belongs to detached operation coordination, not a global action factory.
Retain private worker process dispatch and construction; move Cobra decoration to CLI, lifecycle/persistence to operationrun, snapshot projection to output.
Split user-facing recovery, exact native readback, receipt observation, worker liveness, and result reconciliation; preserve their distinct identities and never reissue accepted writes.

non_go_dispositions.scope: AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, maintained architecture and build references
non_go_dispositions.reason: Teach the new common model and replace content-only migration guidance; do not establish competing instructions in the proposal.
Preserve public command facts; regenerate marked artifacts rather than editing them manually.

non_go_dispositions.scope: .github, scripts, installer assets, bundled agent guidance
non_go_dispositions.reason: Keep cross-platform execution/build/security checks and source/runtime separation; no speculative deletion from file counts.
Move pure tests with owners, retain app.Run integration tests, and require replacement coverage before any removal.

limits: Every current non-test Go package directory receives a structural decision, not a claim that every function or test was reviewed.
A source file with several targets requires symbol-level extraction under its stated ownership rule; this is not authorization to duplicate the file.
Package and dependency names describe the approved target, not completed migration; implementation-status.md records subsequent execution and verification.
Do not infer deleted-file or line-count savings from package consolidation; required behavior survives under a named owner.
Unreproduced correctness concerns from the pilot remain separate from the structural change.
